newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: INTEL SAYS CZECHS SHORTLISTED FOR PLANT.
newsitem.headline: INTEL SAYS CZECHS SHORTLISTED FOR PLANT.

text.p: The Czech Republic is on a short list of countries which Intel Corp. is evaluating as a possible location for a greenfield computer microchip plant, a local spokeswoman for the company said on Monday.

"There are a number of countries on the short list of possible locations including the Czech Republic," Sarka Klofacova, who represents Intel in the Czech Republic, told Reuters reading a statement approved by the company's U.S. headquarters.
"We will continue to evaluate all options. We have made no decision yet," the statement added.

Intel was responding to an unsourced report over the weekend by the Czech daily newspaper Pravo which said the company was looking to build a $300-500 microprocessor plant in the Czech Republic, Egypt or Portugal.
Klofacova said that Intel was looking at options in "Europe, the Middle East, and Asia in terms of suitability for direct investment". She declined to elaborate further on the company's plans.

Pravo said Intel was seeking tax holidays and other incentives, but would generate for the Czech government up to 12 billion crowns in revenue over eight years. It said the plant would initially employee 3,000 people and as many as 9,000 at full capacity.
Industrial areas near the Czech cities of Plzen and Pardubice were under consideration, the Pravo report said.
Matsushita has just opened a $66 million Panasonic television plant in the Borska Pole industrial park near Plzen, one of the largest greenfield investment's to date in the Czech Republic.
